Need for regulation of online matrimonial and dating platforms.
details:
Ms. Swati Maliwal : 
I seek to raise an issue
affecting thousands across our country - the lack of regulation of online
matrimonial and dating platforms. These platforms have helped many find
companionship and life partners. However, a deeply concerning pattern is
emerging. In Hyderabad, a 42-year-old widower, a man, who had already lost his
wife, went on a matrimonial platform hoping to rebuild his life. Instead, he
was emotionally manipulated and lured into a fake crypto investment leading to
an ultimate loss of ₹86 lakh. And this is not an isolated case. In Delhi,
a man was recently arrested for duping over 700 women on dating apps by posing
as a US-based model. Even government employees, professionals, educated people
all are falling victim to fraud, blackmail and even violence through these
sites.? Anyone can create a fake profile. There is no mandatory identity
verification, no accountability of platforms, no real-time fraud detection.
These companies earn Crores. But when fraud happens, they simply say ?Use at
your own risk.?? If we do not act now, these platforms will become hunting
grounds for criminals. I therefore demand the followings from the Government: (i)??? Mandatory
KYC verification for all users. (ii)???? Legal liability of platforms in case
of fraud. (iii)???? AI-based monitoring of suspicious behavior. (iv) Immediate
grievance redressal mechanisms. (v)?? Strong coordination with cybercrime
agencies. People come to these sites seeking trust and companionship. They must
not leave with trauma and loss. The time for stronger safeguards is now. I urge
the Government to look into this.
(ENDS)
?????????
